findings.title: Delete and Pause menu items can never render in the alert list view
findings.body: The PR removes all ruler API fetches from the list view, so AlertRuleMenu is now rendered with `rulerRule === undefined` there (GrafanaRuleListItem passes only `promRule` to RuleActionsButtons.V2, which passes `rulerRule={rule}` = undefined to AlertRuleMenu). However, the Delete menu item is still gated on `canDelete && rulerRule` (line 165) and the Pause item on `canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` (line 123). Since rulerRule is always undefined in the list view, these items never render, even though the newly added `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` checks for Delete and Pause were clearly added to enable them (they are otherwise dead code). This is a functional regression: users who could previously delete or pause Grafana-managed rules from the alert list (when ruler rules were fetched) can no longer do so. The render conditions need promRule-based alternatives (e.g. a prom-rule-based pause menu item and a delete path that uses the identifier instead of the rulerRule).

findings.title: Silence menu item is shown in the list view but the silence drawer never opens
findings.body: In the list view, RuleActionsButtons is rendered with only `promRule` (no `rule`/RulerRuleDTO), so `canSilence` is now computed via the new grafana prom-rule abilities and the 'Silence notifications' menu item does render. But clicking it only calls `setShowSilenceDrawer(true)`, and the drawer is conditionally rendered as `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer && <SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer rulerRule={rule} .../>`. With `rule` undefined, this condition is always false, so clicking 'Silence notifications' silently does nothing. The silence drawer needs to be adapted to work from a GrafanaPromRuleDTO (or the menu item must be hidden) — as shipped, users get a clickable action that has no effect.

findings.title: GrafanaRuleListItem rendered without a React key inside rules.map()
findings.body: The switch in `rules.map()` previously rendered `<GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} ...>`; the replacement `<GrafanaRuleListItem rule={rule} groupIdentifier={groupIdentifier} ... />` drops the `key` prop (the other branches, e.g. DataSourceRuleLoader and UnknownRuleListItem, still set `key={key}`). Rendering array children without keys makes React reconcile by index, which can cause stale/wrong item state when the list grows via infinite scroll or when items are removed, and produces a React warning. The `key={key}` should be restored on the GrafanaRuleListItem element.

findings.title: Refactor drops the federated-rule-group immutability check for useAllAlertRuleAbilities consumers
findings.body: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` (still used by `useAlertRuleAbility`, which backs the non-V2 RuleActionsButtons, RuleDetails, etc.) previously computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` so that rules in federated (Mimir cross-tenant) rule groups were treated as immutable — Edit/Delete/Update were not supported. The refactor delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, which hardcodes `const isFederated = false;` with only a TODO comment. As a result, federated cloud rules now show Edit/Delete/Pause as supported and allowed based on folder permissions, where previously they were disabled. This is a behavior regression for Mimir federated rule groups; either the federated check needs to be preserved for the CombinedRule path or this should be explicitly tracked as a known limitation before merge.

findings.title: Rule view link lost the returnTo query parameter
findings.body: The deleted GrafanaRuleListItem built the item href as `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`, so navigating to a rule's view page preserved a way back to the list context. The new GrafanaRuleListItem builds `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` with no returnTo, so users clicking a rule in the list lose the back-navigation context that the previous implementation provided. If this drop is not intentional, the `{ returnTo }` option should be restored.

findings.title: Stale comment and variable name reference ruler preloading that no longer happens
findings.body: The `useGrafanaGroupsGenerator` cache-population block still carries the comment 'This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules, but it improves the UX / Because the user waits a bit longer for the initial load...' and the local variable is still named `cacheAndRulerPreload`, but this PR removed the `alertRuleApi.util.prefetch('getGrafanaRulerGroup', ...)` call, so no ruler preloading occurs anymore. The comment and name now describe behavior that doesn't exist and will mislead future maintainers.
